newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin sees first govt bond in years in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin sees first govt bond in years in 1997.

text.p: Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Monday the government is likely to issue government bonds for the first time in almost 10 years in 1997.
Amnuay told Reuters the government aim in issuing such bonds would be to create a benchmark for Thailand's fledgling secondary debt market.
He said he will propose amended draft legislation by end-January which will allow the government to issue bonds even though it does not face a budget deficit.
If approved by the cabinet, the draft has to go before parliament before it can become law.
"We need some depth in our money market. How can we develop our debt market without long-term bonds?" Amnuay said.
"I believe we should be able to issue government bonds again within this year because every side seems to agree to the idea," he told Reuters.
Current Thai law prohibits the government from issuing bonds unless it is to finance a fiscal deficit -- which Thailand has not faced in the past 10 years.

Amnuay said the government will use the proceeds from the issues to re-lend to state enterprises for important projects. "I don't think we will have any fiscal deficit. So the government will let state enterprises borrow this money from us," he said.
Thailand has a balanced 1996/97 budget (October-September) of 984 billion baht ($39.36 billion).
